Then she called her own sheep. They heard and ran to her. Then the god became afraid. "Mother, I took them. Do not strike me!" Then she spoke: "Bring me the wool and a gift!" Then the god brought the Mother wool and a gift, and she led her own sheep home.

Now, gods, givers of good things, come to us! Sit down in the middle; drink the wine. And become joyful, gods, in your hearts. Father Sky, come with your daughter Dawn. Fire, bring the Sun, the Waters. Mother Earth, listen to us. Gods, you slew the serpent with thunder. You freed the waters and the cattle from the stone. You set the sun, the stars above. We sing your great fame. Give us victory and might. Now, protect us from the wolf and from sores. Your might is imperishable.

Lead us and our brothers to the light. Now, guard our fences from the wolf. May your brightness not go away from us.

The father went away. His son grew up and became a warrior, and in his youth he grew strong. Then the father arrived with a troop, and the warrior stepped against him: "Warrior, who is your father?" "My father went away. Men say: 'He vanished.'" "I am your father." "I do not trust you. Lift your spear!" Then he said: "I shall strike down my son, or my son will strike me down." Then the two struck. The father's spear bored through his heart. The warrior fell to the earth and spoke: "Now, father, I have come to know you." Then he died. He cried aloud and lay down beside him: "Your fame will be imperishable. May death seize me!"

The son of a man came to love the daughter of the master. He spoke to his own father. Then the father said to his own brother: "Let us go to the master, and let us seek his daughter for my son." Then the two went, and led ten cattle before them. They arrived, and the master saw them and said: "Sit down, guests." They sat down, and he set mead before them. Then the guest said: "We have come; we seek your daughter. The bride-price of your daughter is ten cattle." The master listened, and said: "I am listening to you. Drink the wine, and I shall speak with my wife."

A swift god stole the cattle of Sky in the night and drove them to the field. Then he drove them to the river, and the cattle were swimming. Then he hid them in the marsh. An old man was sitting at the door. The old man was listening well. He saw the god and recognized him. At dawn Sky looked at his own cattle and did not see them. Then he called the old man: "Who has taken my cattle?" Then the old man said: "The god took them. I saw him." Then the Father was saying: "Swift god, you stole my cattle. Lead them back!" Then the swift god became afraid and led the cattle back, and he gave two bulls. "Father, do not strike me!" Then the Father said: "Live! And do not steal again."

In the house of the clan chief the warriors divided the cattle. The chief took the first share, and he gave bulls to the young men. He who had guarded the enclosure, to him they gave two sheep. Then the young men praised him: Giver of good things, may your fame be imperishable! He said: Cattle are the fame of men. Whoever drives them from the enemy, may he receive his share.
